title: Al-Qahhar, the Subduer
hook: the Subduer, over whom nothing prevails
tomorrow: Jordan's grandma gave them paint and wants nothing back. why?

segments.voice: Yesterday, al-Ghaffar: the Ever-Forgiving, and a servant who comes back and comes back. Again and again. Today, the problem that's bigger than you.

Some problems arrive as a form: a permit, a lease, a sign-off from someone you'll never meet. Amira's wall just got one. The building's owner has to approve the mural, and nobody knows when he'll answer, or if. Yesterday asked: now what? The Qur'an has a man with a far bigger wall in front of him. His name is Yusuf, the same name as Amira's dad, and he's in prison for something he didn't do.
screen: `A SIGN-OFF YOU CAN'T FORCE.` → `NOW WHAT?` → `YUSUF, IN PRISON.`

segments.voice: Yusuf has every reason to think the prison is the strongest thing in his life. Instead, he turns to the two men locked up with him and asks, in Pickthall's words: "O my two fellow-prisoners! Are divers lords better, or Allah the One, the Almighty?" That last word is today's name. Al-Qahhar: the Subduer, the One over whom nothing prevails. Pickthall renders it the Almighty. Not the guards, not the king, not the walls. Notice what Yusuf does and doesn't do. He doesn't pretend the cell isn't real. He keeps being himself inside it: he listens, he explains dreams, he asks to be remembered to the king. He does his part, and leaves the part he can't move to the One nothing prevails over. The tradition gives this week a short line for the same balance. A man asked the Prophet, peace be upon him, whether to tie his camel or trust Allah, and the answer, in paraphrase from Tirmidhi: tie it, and trust. And the Qur'an adds a promise about size: "Allah tasketh not a soul beyond its scope." So here's the thing to say to a friend tonight: the too-big thing is real, and so is the One who is bigger. Your job is the rope on the camel. The rest isn't on your back.
screen: `ARE DIVERS LORDS BETTER?` · `AL-QAHHAR: NOTHING PREVAILS OVER HIM.` · `TIE YOUR CAMEL, AND TRUST.` · then, large: `NOTHING PREVAILS OVER HIM.`

segments.voice: On a scrap of paper, write the thing that feels too big this week in a few words. Fold it once and set it face down beside you. For the sit, keep your hands open and empty in your lap, and let it lie there, put down for now.
screen: `WRITE THE TOO-BIG THING.` · `FOLD IT. SET IT DOWN.` · `OPEN HANDS.`

segments.voice: Al-Qahhar: the Subduer, the One over whom nothing prevails. Yusuf named Him from inside a prison cell.
For the road: nothing prevails over him, so tie the rope and set the rest down. See you tomorrow.

howItsDone: Muslims speak of tawakkul, trust in Allah alongside effort, and the 'tie your camel' hadith is one way it's taught; in the Qur'an al-Qahhar is paired with 'the One'.

fork.setup: your family's lease renewal is stuck with a landlord who won't reply. what does today's teaching suggest first?
options: do the part that's yours, one clear message, then set the rest down.
do nothing at all; if it's meant to work out, it will by itself.
message every day until he answers; it's all on you to force it.
fork.reveal: tie the camel, and trust. effort and trust together, the way Yusuf did his part inside the prison and left the walls to al-Qahhar.

original.note: Arabic: the Subduer, over whom nothing prevails. in Yusuf's question in surah 12.

trapdoor: what you thought: the Subduer sounds like a God who crushes people.
what it means: al-Qahhar is the One nothing prevails over, which is why Yusuf can name Him from a cell and not be crushed by it.
what a scholar hears: Qur'an 12:39, where Pickthall renders al-Qahhar 'the Almighty'; Tirmidhi 2517 on tying the camel; Qur'an 2:286.
guess: the One over whom nothing at all prevails
the One who punishes every wrong at once
the One who wins each argument with words

chat.says: owner hasn't answered in a week. i've emailed three times. should i just show up at his house?
options: Send one clear, kind note, then let it sit. Tie the camel; the rest isn't yours to force.
Show up. If you don't control every step yourself, nothing is ever going to happen.
Stop trying at all. If Allah wants the mural, it'll happen without you doing a thing.
chat.meaning: Tie the camel, and trust: do your part well, then set down what's too big. Nothing prevails over al-Qahhar, including a slow inbox.
